title: IIT Madras Students' Crewless Vessel Wins Global Njord Challenge in Norway
excerpt: Team Aritra beat 22 teams from nine countries at the autonomous ship competition in Trondheim, building on its 2023 podium finish.
body:
• Team Aritra, a group of ocean engineering students from IIT Madras, won the 2026 Njord Challenge in Trondheim, Norway — an international competition testing crewless vessels in real maritime conditions.
  • The team scored 90.42 points overall, finishing more than 10 points ahead of 22 rival teams from nine countries, including Turkiye, Poland, Canada, Japan and Norway.
  • The winning crew — Aarav Patel, S. Gurukesav and Madhava Sai — built on the team's 2023 debut, when a different cohort finished third globally and won the Sustainability Award.
  • The victory marks IIT Madras' growing programme in marine autonomous systems, with applications from coastal surveillance to oceanographic research.

A Decisive Win in Trondheim

A team of ocean engineering students from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras has won the 2026 Njord Challenge, an international competition in Norway that puts autonomous surface vessels through their paces in real-world maritime conditions.

Team Aritra secured the overall championship with 90.42 points, finishing more than 10 points clear of MYS YAVUZ from Turkiye (79.90), with AGH Solar Boat from Poland (79.63) in third. The competition, organised by the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) and held in Trondheim from August 10 to 14, brought together 23 teams and 150 participants from nine countries — India, Turkiye, Norway, Poland, Canada, Japan, Spain, Croatia and Scotland.

The winning team was represented by Aarav Patel, S. Gurukesav and Madhava Sai, who led the development and deployment of the autonomous surface vessel, mentored by IIT Madras' Marine Autonomous Vessels (MAV) Laboratory and faculty members Abhilash Sharma and MA Atmanand.

What the Boats Had to Do

Autonomous surface vessels — boats that operate without a human crew on board — were evaluated on autonomous docking, collision avoidance, manoeuvring and pathfinding, along with technical inspection, reporting and presentation. This year's edition added a surprise autonomy challenge, testing how effectively teams could adapt their systems to an unfamiliar situation on the water.

The applications go well beyond sport. Crewless vessels have potential uses in coastal and harbour surveillance, port and strategic infrastructure monitoring, environmental and oceanographic data collection, and hydrographic surveys — persistent maritime operations where reducing the need for continuous human presence improves both safety and efficiency.

Building on 2023

The victory continues a trajectory. A different cohort of Team Aritra students finished third globally at the 2023 Njord Challenge and won the Sustainability Award, establishing IIT Madras on the competition's map. This year's team turned that promise into a championship.

Prof. V. Kamakoti, Director of IIT Madras, met the students and congratulated them on the victory, urging them to take their work forward and ensure their expertise benefits the country.

"Our vision at the Marine Autonomous Vessels Laboratory is to help build the capabilities that India will need as marine autonomy becomes increasingly important. We hope projects such as Team Aritra will excite more students to explore marine robotics."

— Abhilash Sharma, Associate Professor of Ocean Engineering, IIT Madras

Why It Matters

India has one of the world's longest coastlines and a growing stake in maritime security, offshore energy and ocean science — all domains where autonomous vessels are moving from research labs to real deployment. A student team beating established university programmes from maritime nations like Norway and Japan signals that India's marine robotics pipeline is maturing fast.

For the diaspora, it is another data point in a familiar story: Indian engineering students competing — and winning — on the world stage. From 2023's third place to 2026's championship, Team Aritra's arc is the kind of steady, earned excellence that needs no embellishment.
